(Capacity: 18,119) |champion= |tourney=[[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |tourney_result = Second Round}} {{2021–22 American Athletic Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2021–22 Memphis Tigers men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Memphis]] in the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Tigers were led by fourth-year head coach [[Penny Hardaway]]. The team played their home games at [[FedExForum]] as members of the [[American Athletic Conference]]. They finished the season 22–11, 13–5 in [[2021–22 American Athletic Conference men's basketball season|AAC Play]] to finish in 3rd place. They defeated [[2021–22 UCF Knights men's basketball team|UCF]] and [[2021–22 SMU Mustangs men's basketball team|SMU]] to advance to the championship game of the [[2022 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|AAC tournament]] where they lost to [[2021–22 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 9 seed in the West Region, where they defeated [[2021–22 Boise State Broncos men's basketball team|Boise State]] in the First Round before losing in the Second Round to [[2021–22 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga]]. ==Previous season== The [[2020–21 Memphis Tigers men's basketball team|Tigers]] finished the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21 season]] 20–8, 11–4 in [[2020–21 American Athletic Conference men's basketball season|AAC play]], finishing in third place. They entered as the No. 3 seed in the [[2021 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|AAC tournament]], where they would lose to No. 2 seed [[2020–21 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston]] in the semifinals. They were selected as a No. 1 seed in the [[2021 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]]. The Tigers would go on to win the tournament, their second overall, and first since [[2002 National Invitation Tournament|2002]]. ==Offseason== On June 11, 2021, speculation emerged that Penny Hardaway was a candidate for multiple head coaching jobs in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] including his former team, the [[Orlando Magic]].{{Cite web|last=Cordner|first=Jason|date=2021-06-11|title=Penny Hardaway Draws Interest of Several NBA Teams For Head Coach|url=https://thesource.com/2021/06/11/source-sports-penny-hardaway-draws-interest-of-several-nba-teams-for-head-coach/|access-date=2021-06-30|website=The Source|language=en-US}} On June 28, reports emerged that Hardaway had in fact interviewed and emerged as a top candidate for the vacant head coaching job.{{Cite web|last=Cali|first=Mike|date=2021-06-27|title=Report: Penny Hardaway interviewed for Orlando Magic head coaching job and is a "serious candidate"|url=https://www.orlandopinstripedpost.com/2021/6/27/22553215/orlando-magic-penny-hardaway-interview-nba-head-coach|access-date=2021-06-30|website=Orlando Pinstriped Post|language=en}} Two days later, via Instagram, Hardaway confirmed he was not leaving the University of Memphis, and reports emerged that [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|Hall of Fame]] coach [[Larry Brown (basketball)|Larry Brown]] had accepted an offer to be his assistant.{{Cite web|title=Penny Hardaway won't coach Magic, reportedly hires Hall of Famer Larry Brown as Memphis assistant|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/penny-hardaway-wont-coach-magic-reportedly-hires-larry-brown-as-memphis-assistant-034954110.html|access-date=2021-06-30|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en-US}} ===Departing players=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" !
